note.label: Job 30: They That Are Younger Than I Have Me In Derision

precepts.why:
“But now they that are younger than I have me in derision, whose fathers I would have disdained to have set with the dogs of my flock.” This goes into Esau. “And Esau said to Jacob, Feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage; for I am faint: therefore was his name called Edom.” Esau is the one who sold his birthright for pottage, the father of the base people Job describes, whose fathers were not even good enough to sit with Job's animals.

For want and famine they were solitary, fleeing into the wilderness in former time desolate and waste. There is a class, believed to be by Deacon Ikkos or the Bishop, that went into the history of how Esau was chased into the mountains and was eating the lights out of the drawers while the drawers disintegrated on them. These were the masked people. The strength of their hands profited Job nothing, and in them old age was perished.

precepts.text: Job's soul is poured out; the days of affliction take hold of him, his bones are pierced in the night, and God has become cruel to him and opposes himself against him, bringing him to the grave, the house appointed for all living. This is the same situation David was in: the Lord was opposed to him for his sin and did not listen at some point, but after David turned around, the Lord began to listen.
precepts.point: As with a sword in his bones, his enemies reproach him while they say daily, "Where is thy God?" Again he preaches to his soul: "Why art thou cast down? Hope thou in God, for I shall yet praise him, who is the health of my countenance, and my God."

note.label: Psalm 42: Panting After God in the Midst of Affliction

precepts.why:
“As with a sword in my bones, mine enemies reproach me”. Job knew that place: “My bones are pierced in me in the night season: and my sinews take no rest.” “And now my soul is poured out upon me; the days of affliction have taken hold upon me.” He is cast into the mire, become like dust and ashes, and worse: “I cry unto thee, and thou dost not hear me: I stand up, and thou regardest me not. Thou art become cruel to me: with thy strong hand thou opposest thyself against me.” He knows the Lord “wilt bring me to death, and to the house appointed for all living”, the grave.

This is the same situation David was in. The Lord was opposed to him for his sin and did not listen at some point; but after David turned around, the Lord began to listen. That is why David can preach to his own soul, “hope thou in God: for I shall yet praise him”. Punishment for sins drives you back to the Most High: when affliction comes we go back to the Lord, and that is how the Lord gets us back. This is the situation a lot of us end up in if we lose sight of what we are supposed to be doing, which is keeping the commandments.

precepts.text: Job calls himself a brother to dragons, showing that dragons in prophecy stand for men.
precepts.point: They hid in Egypt among the Egyptians. A family that did not look like the people of that land would have been no more hidden there than anywhere else.

note.label: Matthew 2: The Wise Men, Herod's Fear, and the Flight into Egypt

precepts.why:
A dragon in prophecy is not a beast. Job says, “I am a brother to dragons, and a companion to owls.” Job, a man, calls himself a brother to dragons; dragons in prophecy stand for men.

So the great red dragon standing before the woman to devour her child is men, moved by that old serpent, and in Matthew 2 the man standing to devour the child is Herod, seeking the young child to destroy him.

precepts.why: The bottomless pit: what is it and where is it? “They were driven forth from among men,” There was a particular race that was driven forth from among men. “(they cried after them as after a thief;)” We chased them like they stole something. “To dwell in the clifts of the valleys,” Here is the bottomless pit. “in caves of the earth, and in the rocks.” This is the Caucasus mountains of Georgia, Russia. We chased a particular beast, a particular race of men, from among us, like they stole something. “Among the bushes they brayed; under the nettles they were gathered together. They were children of fools, yea, children of base men:” They were children of the lowest types of men on earth. “they were viler than the earth.” Worse than anything on the earth. “And now am I their song, yea, I am their byword.” Because this people came out of the bottomless pit and rose up against us. This whole of Job 30 is prophetic of a particular man who was driven forth from among men to dwell in the clifts of the valleys, who now rose up and came against the people of Job. “They abhor me, they flee far from me, and spare not to spit in my face.” Because he hath loosed my cord, and afflicted me: this particular race would now afflict us; they have let loose the bridle before me: they conquered us, they overthrew us. So the beast that ascendeth out of the bottomless pit is the man that came from the Caucasus mountains of Georgia, Russia, who made war against the two kingdoms and overcame them and killed them. When did this happen? It began in 1453, during the time of the Renaissance, when they rose up against both kingdoms: they got Judah on the east side, and Ephraim and them in the Western Hemisphere.
